content: {"rule": "K-C", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The text grades the D3-vs-C6 collision, in which the witnesses pressed against the defender's Isaiah 7:14 link are the challenger's own Link-6 chain (the sign's bounds at 7:16 and 8:3-4 read together), which is exactly the chain-against-chain situation the rule governs.", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "the sign itself does not state the mechanism", "rule_words": "the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side", "room": "The clause 'the sign itself does not state the mechanism': read one way it is the judge's own ground, letting one verse's own-words silence help withhold determination -- the retired stating-verse test weighed verse by verse; read the other way it is a neutral gloss on the chains' standoff (CR2's 8:8 and 9:6-7 answer vs DR3's bounds-press) that does no verdict-work; I weighed the ground-reading against the gloss-reading and took the ground-reading, since in a one-line verdict each coordinated clause is offered as a basis.", "why": "At a collision the rule requires to be decided by footing alone, the judge's stated basis for UNDERDETERMINED includes what the sign 'itself does not state' -- the exact own-words silence that K-C retires at the judge's seat -- so a single verse's silence was allowed to do verdict-work."}
